Subject: Introducing contracting owners and evaluation sprint plan for Glacier Biotech

Team — looping you in as we formalize the MAP for Glacier Biotech (DEAL-4721). They’re targeting an MSA + SOW signature before the end of September, and they’ve asked for a concrete evaluation program so their security and procurement teams can sign off on timelines.

High-level asks:
- Introduce ownership for terms and redlines (legal) — who will own initial redline and who triages exceptions?
- Share a short evaluation sprint plan (2–3 checkpoints) that procurement/security can attach to the MAP.
- Confirm attachments we can share (SOC 2, data handling, SOW template).

I’ve drafted a one-sheet MAP (attached) with proposed milestones: evaluation kickoff 8/2, security review week of 8/9, commercial redlines 8/16–8/23, SOW finalization 9/2, signature sprint 9/20–9/30. Please flag any timing conflicts.

Thanks — I’ll introduce the Glacier procurement owners in a follow-up with the MAP and a short SOW stub.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft, milestones), Glacier_SecQ-2027.pdf (placeholder, will provide full pack after initial ask)

Ben — thanks for the plan and for the draft MAP. Quick notes from procurement/security:
- We need a named legal contact at Redwood who will accept the first redline and own negotiation cadence.
- Glacier’s security team requires SOC 2 Type II report and any encryption-at-rest details prior to the start of production trials.
- For timelines: our procurement lead (Tom) and our legal (Lila) will need two weeks to review clean redlines; moving any milestone earlier will be difficult.

Can your team confirm the redline owner and when Redwood can provide SOC 2 and a short SOW stub? Also would like to see an evaluation acceptance criteria doc that our engineers can test against during the trial.

Quick notes on process:
- I’ll accept the first redline and consolidate internal comments; please ask Glacier legal to send a clean redline in Word track changes to legal@redwood.ai and cc me.

- If Glacier requires unusual indemnities or data residency clauses, flag them early — that’s the biggest driver of delay.

I’ve attached a redline playbook checklist and our SOW stub (SOW-draft.docx). I’ll be available for a focused redline sync on 8/17 if that helps.

Subject: Evaluation sprint plan and acceptance criteria (draft)

Hi Sofia / Tom — attaching a short evaluation sprint plan and acceptance criteria that we typically attach to MAPs. Highlights:
- Sprint 1 (8/2–8/6): Proof-of-concept connectivity and basic inference validation (latency, basic accuracy).
- Sprint 2 (8/9–8/20): Security and data handling checks (SOC 2 artifacts, encryption, audit logs), plus scaled throughput run.
- Sprint 3 (8/23–9/3): Business-case validation with sample workload; output quality checkpoints and rollback criteria.

Acceptance criteria are explicit per sprint (pass/fail) and we include remediation steps and a 48–72 hour fix window for high-severity issues.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: Evaluation_Sprint_Plan.pdf

I’ll expect the SOW stub and MAP update after you incorporate the 8/16 redline window.
